source_text: Quo recitato Augustinus episcopus dixit: Audite qui nescitis, audite, obsecro uos. deo gratias, quia ipso praesente loquor. causam istam Maximianistarum, quam uolo modo uobis exponere, ubi omnium calumniarum suarum tamquam malarum mercium nauem fregerunt, causam ergo istam Maximianistarum cum totiens obiecissemus in nostra collatione, nihil aduersus eam dicere potuerunt, id est aduersus obiectionem nostram totiens insertam, totiens repetitam, totiens eorum frontibus illisam nihil omnino respondere potuerunt, quia quod responderent non inuenerunt. audite ergo illam diligenter. ecce hic est, audit me. si mentior, redarguat, probare me compellat. gesta quidem ipsa hic non sunt, sed ibi sit causa. feramus quaslibet dilationes, ut ad documenta necessaria ueniamus, si probauero quod dico. si tamen inde dubitat aut, quod absit, dubitare se fingit, quod pace eius dixerim, non communicet, si non probauero. si autem scit iam me uerum dicere et nouit propterea respondere noluisse, quia quod responderet non potuit inuenire, rogo uos, ut ipsi iudicetis quid sit tolerabilius, in honore suo suscipere a se damnatum an fratrem agnoscere non aliquando a se conuictum. intendite, obsecro, audite narrationem.
thought_title: Augustine challenges Emeritus to answer the Maximianist case
orientation: Augustine, the Catholic bishop, is speaking directly to the gathered people in the presence of Emeritus, the Donatist bishop, after Alypius has finished reading the bishops' letter.
pass_a_gloss: Which [having been] read aloud Augustine [the] bishop said: Hear you who do not know, hear, I beseech you. [Thanks] to God, because [with] him present I speak. [The] cause this of [the] Maximianists, which I want now to you to set forth, where of all [the] slanders of their own as of evil wares [the] ship they broke, [the] cause therefore this of [the] Maximianists when so often we had objected in our conference, nothing against it they were able to say, that is against [the] objection of ours so often inserted, so often repeated, so often against their foreheads dashed nothing at all to answer they were able, because what they might answer they did not find. Hear therefore it carefully. Behold here he is, he hears me. If I lie, let him refute [me], [to] prove me let him compel [me]. [The] acts indeed themselves here are not, but there let [the] cause be. Let us bear whatever delays, so that to [the] documents necessary we may come, if I shall have proved what I say. If however from this he doubts or, which [may it be] absent, [to] doubt himself he pretends, which with his peace I would have said, let him not communicate, if I shall not have proved [it]. If however he knows now me [the] truth to speak and knows for this reason to answer [he] was unwilling, because what he might answer he was not able to find, I ask you, that you yourselves judge what is [more] tolerable, in [the] honor of his own to receive [one] by himself condemned or [a] brother to acknowledge not at any time by himself convicted. Attend, I beseech [you], hear [the] narration.

choices.term: calumniarum suarum tamquam malarum mercium nauem fregerunt
choices.english: they broke the ship of all their false accusations as if of bad merchandise
choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of shipwrecked cargo intact, showing the Maximianist case destroyed the Donatists' whole case.
rejected: they wrecked their ship of slanders like a cargo of bad goods
they shattered the vessel of their calumnies as if it were a ship of worthless wares

choices.why: Preserves the vivid physical image of the objection being thrown in their faces repeatedly.

choices.english: Let us bear whatever grace periods
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'grace period' for dilatio, keeping the technical sense of a time limit for return.
rejected: Let us put up with any postponements

choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'communion' in verbal form, keeping the technical sense of Eucharistic fellowship.
rejected: let him be out of communion

choices.term: in honore suo suscipere a se damnatum
choices.english: to receive in his honor one condemned by himself
choices.why: Keeps the paradox of receiving someone back in the same honor after condemning them, which is Augustine's key point.
rejected: to receive in his own honor someone he had condemned
to take back in his honor a man condemned by himself

choices.term: fratrem agnoscere non aliquando a se conuictum
choices.english: to acknowledge a brother never convicted by himself
choices.why: Keeps the contrast between 'condemned by himself' and 'never convicted by himself', which is the heart of the argument.
rejected: to recognize a brother never proven guilty by him
to acknowledge a brother he had never convicted

pass_b_english: When it had been read, Augustine the bishop said: Listen, you who do not know; listen, I beg you. Thanks be to God, because I am speaking with him present. This case of the Maximianists, which I want to set out for you now, is where they broke the ship of all their false accusations as if of bad merchandise. When we had thrown this case of the Maximianists against them so many times in our conference, they could say nothing against it—that is, against our objection so many times inserted, so many times repeated, so many times dashed against their foreheads. They could answer nothing at all, because they found nothing to answer. So listen to it carefully. Here he is; he hears me. If I lie, let him refute me, let him compel me to prove it. The records themselves are not here, but let the case be there. Let us bear whatever grace periods, so that we may come to the necessary documents, if I prove what I say. If, however, he doubts it or—God forbid—pretends to doubt it, and I say this with his leave, let him not be in communion with us if I do not prove it. But if he already knows that I am speaking the truth and knows that he refused to answer because he could find nothing to answer, then I ask you to judge for yourselves which is more tolerable: to receive into his own rank one condemned by him, or to acknowledge a brother not ever convicted by him. Pay attention, I beg you; listen to the account.

problems.why: communicet means 'let him not have communion [with me/us]'; 'communicate' is archaic/unclear for modern readers.
ipso refers to Emeritus, not God; Augustine speaks with Emeritus present.
problems.ruling: ipso praesente follows 'Here he is; he hears me' referring to Emeritus present, not God.

dismissed.quote: broke the ship of all their false accusations as if of bad merchandise
dismissed.why: The ship metaphor is mangled: they broke their ship (of calumnies), not "the ship of accusations."
dismissed.note: The English follows the Latin image correctly: they wrecked the ship of their calumnies, as if it carried bad cargo; the checker only wants a different wording.

dismissed.quote: let him not be in communion with us
dismissed.why: The subject is Augustine, not "us"; "let him not be in communion [with me]" if Augustine fails to prove his case.
dismissed.note: The subject of 'communicet' is Emeritus, not Augustine; 'with us' fairly supplies the Catholic communion Augustine speaks for.
